answer: Each identity posts an 80-credit bond for one cedar nectar feeder, with its serial on a board. It logs sparrow visits and nectar drawn; auditors recompute expected draw as visits times 2 millilitres against the refill. A mismatch over 5 percent, reused serial, or copied log burns the bond. The k-th fake pays 34 credits plus 7 per earlier feeder, so the 1000th pays 7027 and 1000 fakes pay 3,530,500 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-feeder ring fails because one feeder cannot yield visit-depletion pairs for many. An honest keeper pays 34 once, recovers the bond.
